title: Ultralow-Tensile Strain Enables Exciton Funneling and Energy Transfer to Boost MoSe2 Photoluminescence Quantum Yield
authors: Gayatri, Mehdi Arfaoui, Debashish Das, Mateusz Raczyński, Marta Bilska, Piotr Tatarczak, Aleksandra Krystyna Dąbrowska, Tomasz Kazimierczuk, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Piotr Kossacki, Andrzej Wysmołek, Saroj Kumar Nayak, Adam Babiński, Johannes Binder, Maciej R. Molas, Arka Karmakar
abstract: Strain engineering is a powerful route for controlling the exciton dynamics in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures (HSs). The interlayer energy transfer (ET) process is another key factor in controlling the photocarrier relaxation pathways in vdW HSs. In this work, we combine these two processes to achieve an 8-fold enhancement to the relative photoluminescence (PL) quantum yield (QY) in a HS formed from monolayers of ReS2 and MoSe2, separated by a thin hBN interlayer, placed onto an hBN bubble. We achieve this enhancement by applying only 0.1% biaxial tensile strain, which results in efficient exciton funneling and an increased transition dipole moment. Our experimental data are supported by first-principles density-functional theory and coherent transfer-matrix method calculations, ruling out optical interference as the dominant origin of the enhancement. This work provides an innovative route for enhancing the PL QY of vdW materials via interplay between the tensile strain and the ET process.
summary: This research demonstrates that applying minute biaxial tensile strain to a vdW heterostructure ($	ext{ReS}_2/	ext{hBN}/	ext{MoSe}_2$) can dramatically enhance its photoluminescence quantum yield. The enhancement stems from a synergistic effect: the strain funnels excitons toward high-strain regions while simultaneously boosting energy transfer efficiency. This offers a powerful, strain-tunable route for designing high-performance 2D optoelectronic devices.
main_problem: The goal is to enhance the photoluminescence (PL) quantum yield (QY) in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by synergistically combining strain engineering and interlayer energy transfer (ET).
main_result: Applying only a small biaxial tensile strain ($\sim 0.1\%$) enables efficient exciton funneling and boosts the relative PL QY by approximately 8-fold in a $	ext{ReS}_2/	ext{hBN}/	ext{MoSe}_2$ heterostructure.
method: The study combines experimental measurements (PL mapping, Raman spectroscopy, Time-Resolved PL) with theoretical calculations (DFT and coherent transfer-matrix method) to confirm the underlying physical mechanisms.
model_or_system: The physical system is a multilayer vdW heterostructure ($	ext{ReS}_2/	ext{hBN}/	ext{MoSe}_2$) placed on a substrate, where localized tensile strain is induced using $	ext{hBN}$ bubbles. The physics involves exciton dynamics, energy transfer, and strain-dependent band structure modification.
key_observables: PL Quantum Yield (QY) enhancement factor ($\sim 8	imes$), PL redshift (indicating strain), and exciton decay lifetimes ($	au_1, 	au_2$).
important_parameters: Tensile strain ($\sim 0.1\%$), $	ext{hBN}$ spacer thickness ($\sim 12 	ext{ nm}$), and excitation energies ($1.58 	ext{ eV}$ to $2.40 	ext{ eV}$).
main_assumptions: The enhancement mechanism is confirmed to be due to strain-induced funneling and ET, ruling out optical interference effects via TMM calculations.
figures_summary: Figures show AFM images of the bubble structure, Raman maps confirming strain gradients, and PL intensity maps demonstrating localized enhancement at the bubble apex.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by reviewing strain/ET control in vdW materials, presents the experimental setup using engineered $	ext{hBN}$ bubbles, measures strain and PL enhancement, and supports the findings with theoretical modeling of exciton dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, tunable platform for controlling quantum optical properties in 2D materials by coupling mechanical strain to electronic structure and energy transfer pathways, which is highly relevant for quantum light sources.
